input.rationale: Navigation fix after the negative control: the parent question's discriminator mentioned both store shapes and a snapshot cadence that never leaves a committed entry between the last snapshot and the recovered commit index. The cadence half is now measured in both directions (the control shows the gap absent when the snapshot covers the change), so the discriminator keeps only what remains unmeasured — stores other than the in-memory ones used here, in particular commit-tracking stores backed by production storage. No evidence, comparison or conclusion changes.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the same gap and its consequences appear with commit-tracking log stores backed by production storage rather than the in-memory stores used in every measurement, and whether such a store's staging semantics change when the recovered commit index reaches a configuration entry; the cadence direction is measured in both directions, so what remains is store implementation breadth.

investigations.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled, does the NewRaft configuration scan still load every committed configuration entry at or below the commit index the node recovers, so that r.configurations reflects committed membership after restart?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the recovered commit index, and the scan loop starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so committed configuration entries at or below the commit index are never loaded into r.configurations; a restarted node keeps the snapshot configuration only, or an empty configuration when it has no snapshot.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the gap and the consequences measured under it also appear with other log store shapes, in particular a commit-tracking store that is also monotonic and one whose snapshot cadence never leaves a committed configuration entry between the last snapshot and the recovered commit index; both repair paths are now measured, so the remaining question is the breadth of the store and snapshot-cadence assumptions rather than the mechanism.

history.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled, does the NewRaft configuration scan still load every committed configuration entry at or below the commit index the node recovers, so that r.configurations reflects committed membership after restart?
history.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the recovered commit index, and the scan loop starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so committed configuration entries at or below the commit index are never loaded into r.configurations; a restarted node keeps the snapshot configuration only, or an empty configuration when it has no snapshot.
history.discriminator: Restart a node whose commit-tracking store reports a commit index at or above a configuration entry, then compare the recovered commit index, lastApplied, the scan start index and the node's latest configuration with the configuration entry present in the log.

history.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled, does the NewRaft configuration scan still load every committed configuration entry at or below the commit index the node recovers, so that r.configurations reflects committed membership after restart?
history.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the recovered commit index, and the scan loop starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so committed configuration entries at or below the commit index are never loaded into r.configurations; a restarted node keeps the snapshot configuration only, or an empty configuration when it has no snapshot.
history.discriminator: Whether a later configuration entry or an installed snapshot repairs the restarted node's configuration at runtime, and which requests the empty/stale configuration admits (vote and pre-vote membership checks, quorum size, election gating).

history.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled, does the NewRaft configuration scan still load every committed configuration entry at or below the commit index the node recovers, so that r.configurations reflects committed membership after restart?
history.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the recovered commit index, and the scan loop starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so committed configuration entries at or below the commit index are never loaded into r.configurations; a restarted node keeps the snapshot configuration only, or an empty configuration when it has no snapshot.
history.discriminator: Whether an installed snapshot, rather than an arriving configuration entry, restores the recovered configuration at runtime, and whether a legal history exists in which the node stays inside the configuration in force while its log is far enough behind to receive one; the answer needs a node that is behind the leader's log without having lost membership.

investigations.question: Can restoreFromCommittedLogs block NewRaft forever when the recovered committed range needs more FSM batches than the fsmMutateCh buffer, given that runFSM is only started after NewRaft's recovery completes?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs sends commitTuple batches through a 128-slot fsmMutateCh while no consumer exists yet, so a recovered committed range larger than 128 batches (64 entries each by default) makes NewRaft block indefinitely.
investigations.discriminator: Restart with RestoreCommittedLogs and a recovered committed range larger than 128*MaxAppendEntries entries, and observe whether NewRaft returns within a bounded interval.

investigations.question: With an empty or stale configuration after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, which admission checks does the node still apply to RequestVote/RequestPreVote, and what quorum and election gating follow from that state?
investigations.hypothesis: requestVote and requestPreVote skip the membership check when the candidate configuration is empty, so the restarted node grants votes to any candidate, and quorumSize() derived from an empty voter list is 1.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the empty configuration also changes the node's own participation (runFollower election gating) and whether the node accepts AppendEntries from the requester as its leader, both measured rather than derived.

history.question: With an empty or stale configuration after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, which admission checks does the node still apply to RequestVote/RequestPreVote, and what quorum and election gating follow from that state?
history.hypothesis: requestVote and requestPreVote skip the membership check when the candidate configuration is empty, so the restarted node grants votes to any candidate, and quorumSize() derived from an empty voter list is 1.
history.discriminator: Drive the restarted node's vote and pre-vote handlers with a candidate that is absent from its log-recorded configuration and observe granted versus rejected responses.

investigations.question: Does a node restarted with a stale (smaller) configuration after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart commit entries with a quorum that is not a majority of the configuration in force, so that a write acknowledged to a client can be superseded by a leader elected from the true configuration?
investigations.hypothesis: r.configurations.latest, commitment.setConfiguration and quorumSize() all use the recovered configuration, so a node that restarts from a snapshot recording a smaller voter set can win an election against that stale set and commit an entry with acknowledgements from fewer nodes than a majority of the configuration in force; the acknowledged entry is then absent from a leader elected by the configuration in force. A prerequisite that must be verified per measurement is that the restarted node's voter set is still the stale one at the moment it acts as leader, which requires comparing the node's live configuration with the peers it actually replicates to.
investigations.discriminator: Reproduce the multi-node history (bootstrap five voters, demote two so the configuration in force is three voters, snapshot the node under test, re-promote the two voters, commit later traffic so the node's commit-tracking store stages a commit index past that configuration entry, restart the node), then, before and after any leadership change, emit the node's live configuration and its replication peer set together so a repaired configuration cannot be mistaken for a stale one; only after the stale set is confirmed should the acknowledged write be applied and the holders compared against the quorum of the configuration in force.

history.question: Does a node restarted with a stale (smaller) configuration after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart commit entries with a quorum that is not a majority of the configuration in force, so that a write acknowledged to a client can be superseded by a leader elected from the true configuration?
history.hypothesis: r.configurations.latest, commitment.setConfiguration and quorumSize() all use the recovered configuration, so a stale restarted node can win an election against the stale voter set and commit an entry with acknowledgements from fewer than a majority of the true configuration; those holders can then be removed from service while a true majority elects a leader whose log lacks the entry.
history.discriminator: Build a five-voter cluster whose commit-tracking stores are retained, take a snapshot on one follower while the configuration is still the three-voter set, commit the configuration change that adds the other two voters plus later commands on that follower, restart it (stale configuration), remove the serving leader and the two voters not in the stale set so that the stale quorum is reachable, apply a write and record its future result, then remove the stale leader and its acknowledgement partner, restart the remaining voters and record whether the new leader's log and FSM contain the acknowledged write.

investigations.question: Does the public configuration future report the log index of the configuration entry in force, as the IndexFuture contract and the documented latest_configuration_index stat key imply, once a configuration change has been committed?
investigations.hypothesis: GetConfiguration builds a fresh configurationsFuture whose configurations value carries only the latest Configuration, so its latestIndex stays zero: ConfigurationFuture.Index() always returns 0 and Stats copies that 0 into latest_configuration_index even though the node has a committed configuration entry with a real index.
investigations.discriminator: After committing a configuration change, compare the index reported by the change's own future with GetConfiguration().Index() and with Stats()["latest_configuration_index"], and confirm from the log store that the entry at that index is a configuration entry while the live configuration already contains the changed server set.

investigations.question: Can a server that is no longer part of the configuration trigger a leadership change by sending TimeoutNow to a voter, given that the TimeoutNow handler neither verifies the sender nor that a transfer is in progress, while vote requests carrying the leadership-transfer flag suppress the rejection for nodes that already know a leader?
investigations.hypothesis: timeoutNow sets the recipient's state to Candidate and stores candidateFromLeadershipTransfer regardless of who sent the request, so a removed server's message makes the recipient campaign with the transfer flag set; voters then grant their votes although they have a healthy leader, because the leader-availability rejection is skipped when LeadershipTransfer is set, and the serving leader steps down when it observes the higher term.
investigations.discriminator: Remove one node from a three-voter configuration, have that removed node send TimeoutNow over the transport to a surviving follower, and observe the follower's state and term, the serving leader's state, and which node leads afterwards.

investigations.question: Can the leader verification quorum be satisfied by acknowledgements from non-voters while a quorum of the voters in the configuration in force is unreachable?
investigations.hypothesis: verifyLeader registers its future with every entry of the leader's replication map, and that map contains an entry for every server in the configuration, including non-voters; each peer's heartbeat acknowledges the verification, so a heartbeat from a non-voter can raise the vote count to the voter quorum even when no other voter is reachable.
investigations.discriminator: Demote one node of a four-peer cluster so the configuration is three voters plus one non-voter, isolate the leader from the other two voters while leaving the non-voter reachable, confirm that reachability with direct AppendEntries attempts, then call VerifyLeader and observe whether it returns success.

investigations.question: Does a node restarted with the smaller configuration recorded in its snapshot reject vote requests from servers that the configuration in force contains but its recovered voter set does not, so that an eligible participant cannot obtain its vote?
investigations.hypothesis: requestVote's membership rejection tests the candidate against the node's recovered configuration without any notion of the configuration in force, so a server added after the node's snapshot is rejected even though it is a voter everywhere else; the same request shape from a candidate that is inside the recovered set is granted, which isolates the rejection to the membership rule.
investigations.discriminator: Restart a node from a snapshot that records a three-voter configuration while the configuration in force has five voters, then send it vote requests that differ only in the candidate identity: one from a voter in the configuration in force but outside the recovered set, and one from a voter inside the recovered set, both flagged as leadership transfers and with an up-to-date log, and compare the granted results.
